newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan CPC slashes refinery output on crude halt.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan CPC slashes refinery output on crude halt.

text.p: Taiwan's state-owned Chinese Petroleum Corp on Monday slashed production at its Taoyuan refinery to just 34 percent of capacity as a pipeline problem halted crude supplies, officials said.
"Chinese Petroleum has decided to cut the Taoyuan refinery's production to 34 percent of full capacity," a manager at the Taoyuan facility told Reuters by telephone.
"The reduction will allow the refinery to maintain operations with the limited supplies of crude on hand."
The company confirmed early on Monday that it had shut down two offshore crude-offloading systems late last week due to unspecified pipeline problems.
Chinese Petroleum officials told Reuters the refinery had about 407,000 kilolitres crude supplies on hand, enough to keep the refinery running at full speed for only about 10 days.

The Taoyuan refinery manager said engineers would feed about 12,000 kilolitres or 70,000 barrels of crude a day into the facility, effective immediately, just 34 percent of its full capacity consumption of 35,000 kilolitres or 200,000 barrels.
Officials declined to say whether the decision to slow down the refinery's operation indicated a possibility that repairs to the pipeline could take longer than 10 days.
Chinese Petroleum spokesman Fang Yi-shan had told Reuters earlier on Monday that repairs were not expected to take longer than 10 days.
